claims.claim: Holding positions longer would reduce fee drag enough to improve net P/L.
claims.counter_evidence: Only 12 trades; every group is below the 10-trade evidence bar (INCONCLUSIVE). Longer holds also carry more adverse price risk; untested in replay.
claims.evidence: fees/gross 266%; <1h holds net -35.36, >=1h holds net 9.33 (tools/performance_report.py over the closed-position archive).

payload.motivation: Round-trip cost, not direction, decides the result. A trader cuts turnover before tuning signals.
payload.problem: Estimated fees are 266% of gross P/L over 12 closed PAPER trades; trades closed within an hour netted -35.36, longer holds 9.33.
payload.proposed_changes: Step 1 (no runtime change): replay with python -m tools.strategy_compare / tools/backtest_replay.py --min-hold 60 and compare net P/L after fees and slippage on walk-forward windows. Step 2, only if it wins on every window: a separate CRITICAL proposal for a runtime minimum holding time, with tests and an independent audit.
payload.rollback_plan: Step 1 changes nothing. Step 2 would ship behind its own proposal and be reverted by revert commit.
payload.title: Test a minimum holding time: fees exceed the edge
